name: Mateo Park
life: “I still remember a cake that fed three visitors nobody expected.” On Friday, near Breakwater Way, Mateo stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I baked one cake to thank two people. They finally got to cut it while we were all in the same room.
appearance: Mateo has brown hair pinned away from the temples, a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. It usually goes with a watch on a cracked leather band. When somebody else has the floor, Mateo draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
personality: Mateo enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To cut the cake in company.
family: Byron Carbone is Mateo’s cousin. Mateo sets the time to leave. Byron picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *Overdue by a lifetime*, Byron says, “I kept the fine in coins for years. The library wants a story hour instead.”
connections: David Marks. The cake and teapot become a real visit beyond the allotted care tasks.
